text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Soldier kills comrade over use of telephone.
- Communications Minister Limor Livnat quits as liaison between cabinet and Knesset in anger at Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
- U.S.: Hebron riots "safety valve".
- Petty thief's "good deed" saves lives on crowded Tel Aviv beach.
- Cabinet approves top jobs panel.
- Bostoner Rebbe: Quit the smoking habit.
HAARETZ
- Expectation is former Justice Minister Yaacov Neeman will turn down offer by Netanyahu to bring him back into cabinet.
- Cost of Yisrael ba-Aliya demands -- about half a billion shekels in current budget year.
- Two religious Jewish judges to be appointed on 13 July to High Court of Justice.
- Arison group to offer $825-890 million for a third of the shares of Bank Hapoalim.
- Car accidents have a price also for tourism: American Express cancels free insurance for tourists who rent cars in Israel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Syria is accelerating the building of secret hiding places for ballistic missiles.
- Israeli government offers first draft of 4 billion shekel budget cut in 1998.
- Dollar reaches new record -- 3.437 shekels.
MAARIV
- Ariel Sharon to finance ministry; Moshe Katzav to national infrastructure ministry; and Yehoshua Matza to tourism ministry.
- Storm in prime minister's office: Intention to investigate eight workers by polygraph.
